Everyone on the PC shares the same data.

### What's changed
- **One set of data for every Windows account.** Templates, clients, people, settings and sign-ins are now kept in `C:\ProgramData\ID Card Printing Software`, shared by every Windows account on the PC. Before, each Windows account had its own data, so signing in to Windows as someone else, or Windows starting with a temporary profile after a restart, opened an empty program with the `admin` / `admin` sign-in. Each person still signs in to the program with their own username and password.
- **Your data moves across by itself.** The first time a Windows account runs this version, its data moves into the shared folder. If the shared folder already has data of its own, the program asks once which to keep; the other copy stays on the PC as a file.
- **Two Windows accounts signed in at once.** The program runs in whichever account opened it first, and cards print from there. The other account's window shows the same screens. If the first account signs out, the program carries on printing in the other one. Install the card printer for all users.
- **Starts for anyone who signs in.** If **Start automatically** was ticked in the setup, the program now starts when anyone signs in to Windows, not just the person who installed it.
- **Resetting the admin sign-in needs a Windows administrator.** Every Windows account can open the shared data, so `--reset-admin` now asks for an administrator's permission.
- **Updates close the program everywhere.** Setup now closes the program in every Windows account before installing, and the print queue carries on only once the new version is running.

Existing installs keep all their templates, clients and people.

### Updating
An administrator will see **Version 3.0.12 is available** at the top of the program — choose **Update now**. Or download the setup below and run it over the top.

### New install
Download **ID-Card-Printing-Software-Free-Setup-3.0.12.exe** below and run it. The setup isn't code-signed, so the first time Windows may show *Windows protected your PC*: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**, then **Yes**.
